To calculate the SIP amount after 30 years with a 10% step-up every year, we use the formula for compounded annual growth:

Amount in year n = Initial SIP × (1 + Step-up rate)^(n - 1)

Here:

Initial SIP = 2000

Step-up rate = 10% = 0.10

Duration = 30 years

Let's calculate it:

Amount in year 30 = 2000 × (1 + 0.10)^(30 - 1)
= 2000 × (1.10)^29

Calculating:

1.10 raised to the power of 29 is approximately 15.91.

Thus:
Amount in year 30 = 2000 × 15.91 = 31,820 INR.

After 30 years, the SIP amount will be ₹31,820 per month.

Hi Akshat!

Thanks for bringing these videos. Here’s a thought for your SIP calculation.

10K for 30 Years = ₹1,20,000 p.a.

Value of 1.2L after 20yrs = ₹21,400 p.a.

Am I missing something?

I think better is to look at risk statistics like Sharoe ratio, Sortino ratio, Std deviation, Alpha, Beta, R squared etc. Also look at churning ratio. And then look at long term returns of the fund scheme, like returns of 3 yr, 5 yr, 10 yr. Finally, observe the volatility in ranks of long term returns of various timeframe.
